patch_description:
This approach transitions from discrete point-based evaluation approximations to exact continuous curve line integrals utilizing a 3-point Gaussian Quadrature scheme. This computes precise path lengths (F1), school proximity repulsions (F2), and base signal attritions (F3) natively along each segment, perfectly simulating the evaluator.

Because the system inherently minimizes the multiplied combined objective MOP = F1 * F2 * F3, computing explicit analytic integrated gradients for `log(F1) + log(F2) + log(F3)` ensures an optimal update direction unaffected by the huge numerical scaling discrepancies among the three metrics. 

To overcome potential saddle points or local topological minima (e.g. passing symmetrically above or below the school), it relies on a multi-start strategy. Four separate initial trajectory shapes (straight line, mathematically bowing upwards, mathematically bowing downwards, and initially biased towards the target base station) are optimized with an annealed Adam optimizer for 1500 local steps each. The outcome with the mathematically lowest final integrated objective cost is definitively selected and returned.
